system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
These 2 questions belong together and follow one another in the test booklet.

## Question 1

A. WITHOUT using any triangle tiles, place 4 tiles so that 1/2 of a square shape is black. Then shade in the square below to show what you did with your tiles.

Shade in Here

[Image: Square grid]

Figure, described in words:
Under the heading "Shade in Here", a large square is divided into a 2 by 2 grid of 4 smaller congruent squares. Each of the 4 smaller squares has dotted diagonal lines connecting opposite corners, dividing each square into 4 congruent triangles.

## Question 2

B. Place 8 tiles so that 5/8 of the rectangle shape is black. Then shade in the rectangle below to show what you did with your tiles.

Shade in Here

[Image: Rectangular grid]

Figure, described in words:
Under the heading "Shade in Here", a rectangle is divided into a 2 by 4 grid of 8 smaller squares (2 rows and 4 columns). Each of the 8 squares has dotted diagonal lines connecting opposite corners, dividing each square into 4 congruent triangles.

Answer each of the 2 questions.

answer_1.description: Your answer to question 1, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_1.title: Answer 1

answer_2.description: Your answer to question 2, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_2.title: Answer 2

output.answer_1: Use 4 square tiles arranged in a 2 by 2 pattern: place 2 black square tiles in the top row and 2 white square tiles in the bottom row. In the drawing, shade the 2 small squares in the top row of the large square black, leaving the 2 small squares in the bottom row unshaded. Two of the four equal parts are black, so 1/2 of the square is black.
output.answer_2: Use 8 square tiles arranged in 2 rows of 4: place 5 black square tiles and 3 white square tiles. In the drawing, shade black the 4 squares in the top row and the first square of the bottom row, leaving the other 3 squares of the bottom row unshaded. That gives 5 black squares out of 8, so 5/8 of the rectangle is black.
